summary: AstroSurvive is a 3D first-person Martian outpost survival game designed for kids ages 7–12 to experience real space engineering trade-offs. Grounded in NASA's DONKI space weather API and OSDR astronaut health research, players balance power, oxygen, and radiation shielding across five Martian days (Sols) where every survival decision carries a tangible resource cost.
details:
Playable Windows Build (ZIP) : https://drive.google.com/file/d/1k23yc0QLGG2ce0FZH_CwL-iQxZLHRpdv/view?usp=sharing

Built in Unity 6 (C#), AstroSurvive places young learners in a 3D Martian outpost where they must survive 5 Sols (Martian days) by managing three competing resources: Global Power, Oxygen, and Radiation Shielding. At the start of each Sol, the game queries NASA's DONKI API for real solar flare activity (with an embedded local JSON dataset as an offline fallback). When a solar storm hits, players physically toggle the protective shield dome or interact with solar arrays and hydroponic greenhouses to balance power and oxygen—where every choice carries a real engineering trade-off and displays a simplified NASA OSDR/RadLab scientific fact.
